items.title: Every UI element is a named asset
items.detail:
Apply the rule across schemas/asset-types.json, the web and Android ports, the 39 starter assets and the conformance fixtures.

- Two tiers: element assets (button, slider, toggle, input, icon, label...) and parent assets (toolbar, menu, nav, app menu, dialog, container, window). A standalone element in a layout is its own named asset; groups only exist inside a parent asset.
- Namespaced ids for every asset (e.g. axf.button.save, axf.toolbar.editor); layouts and parents reference ids.
- Split instance (label, icon, action, state) from skin (style asset + theme tokens).
- Slots with type contracts in layout regions and parents; hot-swap and drag-and-drop = rebinding a slot to a compatible asset id.
- Kernel unchanged (open type registry).

items.title: Plugin manager + settings tabs for every app (Fable rebuild)

Every app compiled by the build engine ships the settings interface and lib-settings. The Opus version is the console plugin `plugin-manager` (web console only: four views cards/table/detail/dependency graph in four layouts Studio/Mission control/Terminal/Catalog, default context-menu link, dependencies in detail, opens each plugin's UI and settings, logs, files, install & uninstall). Remove it first with its uninstall script (uninstall.mjs --all --publish), then build the cross-port version following plugin-lifecycle@1 (Android kernel + every app the build engine compiles), keeping the UI-editor rules (last save wins per key; reload current values on open/load/focus).

items.title: Port engine: bring a non-AXF app onto AmberX AXF (bake or rebuild)
items.detail:
Runs the ports that claude-project parks (pending items port-<name>, manifest x.port, plan in the project at _claude/memory/docs/port-to-axf.md). Brett chose: ask each time between the two ways.

- bake: keep the codebase, run axf init into it (react-ts / next-ts / android-compose), then move its look and chrome into asset@1 assets step by step (colour/style themes, menus, toolbars, nav, dialogs, layout with region slots); UI reads engine tokens only (THEMING.md). Old styles go as each piece moves.
- rebuild: new AXF app from the closest boilerplate (axf boilerplates), old code kept alongside as reference, rebuilt feature by feature on assets/libraries/plugins.

Deliver: axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild (analysis report: what maps to which asset types, libraries, plugins; then staged codemods like ui-port.mjs does for UI kits), console + MCP drivers, manifest relation none -> built-on when it starts, fixtures/tests. First real targets: xGallery (MossesX/xGallery, React 19 + Express + SQLite) and whatever claude-project parks.

items.title: lib-clone: any AXF app clones its own install with current data
items.detail:
Turn xGallery's New project wizard (MossesX/xGallery: server/src/routes/newproject.ts, src/pages/dev/newproject/NewProjectWizard.tsx, kit/new-project.mjs) into an AXF library so every app built on AXF can clone its install into a new project. Brett: keep the xGallery wizard as is and make it a library for AXF.

What the xGallery wizard does today (reuse the design): renamed copy from the kit, GitHub repo, per-project deploy key installed on the VPS + Actions secrets (VPS_SSH_KEY, ADMIN_PASSWORD, HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN), Hostinger DNS for site + dev panel, Claude GitHub app access, push main, wait for the site deploy, push panel, wait, first-session prompt; resumable, no secrets stored.

New for the library: clone WITH current data (database snapshot + media/files, consistent copy, secrets and sessions stripped, owner reset), the copy gets its own project.manifest.json + _claude/ (claude-project), cross-port contract (web + Android) for the clone action exposed through the interop gate (default-deny), a settings tab (plugin manager rules: no own settings screen), console + MCP drivers. Open questions for Brett at build time: which data is copied by default, and whether the clone keeps users/members.

items.title: Plugin conflict alarm + tracked AI patches + installed add-ons list
items.detail:
Brett, Oct 18 2026 (parked as unsafe: AI patching and cascading uninstalls need design and review before anyone builds it):

1. When a plugin could potentially conflict with another plugin, raise a developer alarm (alerts library, source conflicts) shown as an expandable row grid like the Systems check grid: same kinds of details per row, fix instructions and external links.
2. Each conflict row has 3 badges/actions: (a) uninstall a plugin - choose which one; (b) ignore; (c) use AI to patch the conflict. The patch must NOT alter any plugin source.
3. Patches are tracked and listed in an Installed add-ons list that covers plugins, add-ons, modules, libraries and patches. Installing a patch is tracked and the patch can be removed.
4. Removing a patch uninstalls every conflicting plugin it patched; those plugins must then be reinstalled.

Builds on: alerts library (conflicts source, diagnostics: same asset id / setting key / settings tab from two named modules; plugins:dup ids on the server), plugin-lifecycle@1 (install/uninstall scripts, backups), plugin-manager (Fable, pending), agent manager add-ons (agent-addon@1 install/uninstall tracking), axf.llm@1 for the AI patch.
Open questions for Brett at build time: what counts as a potential conflict beyond the runtime diagnostics (routes, capability services, settings keys, assets, nav ids, CSS prefixes, data dirs?); where patches live (an overlay layer the console applies at load, never the plugin folder); whether removing a patch should back up the plugins first and offer one-tap reinstall.

items.title: Agents + assistant sessions hosted on axHub (one host for every app)
items.detail:
Brett, Oct 20 2026: agents (Build Pilot's pilot-assembler, Mosses and every agent-definition@1 agent) and AI assistant live sessions should run on axHub, not inside each app. Build Pilot, the Dev Console and the phone apps become clients.

- axHub gets an agent + session host: runs turns, owns live-session@1 event logs (sessions survive app restarts and browser closes), per-agent memory, provider keys in axHub's vault, hub permissions for who may use which agent.
- Apps plug in through what the Fable rebuilds left open: the live-session host registry (`axf.live-host@1` / `register_host`, today a typed `axhub` placeholder in the console and Build Pilot), Build Pilot's assembly backend (BP_AGENT=local|console|off → add `axhub`), and the kernel placeholders `axf.agents`, `axhub.agent`.
- axHub never depends on AXF (decision): the host speaks the contracts over its API (AXPP), with an AXF adapter on the AXF side (lib-hub).
- The assembly gate (pilot-assembly@1) stays in Build Pilot: axHub only proposes ops; Build Pilot checks and builds. Manual mode unaffected.
- Needs the axHub repo (MossesX/axHub) attached.

Until then: Build Pilot runs its agent locally (Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026), the console's assistant hosts its own sessions.

items.title: Console Android app: Pilot + axHub tabs (web views, everything in the app)
items.detail: Brett, Oct 20 2026: the Android console app needs Pilot and axHub tabs like the web console's App tabs plugin. Option A: every tab runs inside the app — Build Pilot (pilot.amberxai.com) and axHub (axhub.amberxai.com, Apps page + approvals) in locked-down in-app web views; nothing ever opens the phone's browser. Fable (the Compose AppShell gains the shared page slots the web shell has). Broken into small builds (sub prompts) so it can be worked on a little at a time; each sub prompt stands alone and leaves the app building.

subPrompts.text: 1. Compose AppShell page slots: `app.frame.top` (above the banner) and `app.frame.cover` (over the shell) as framework slots in `axf-ui` (`Slots.kt`, same names and contract as `framework/react/components/Slots.tsx`); kernel `ExtensionPoints` entry so modules contribute; fixture-free but unit-tested; wire the Android console showcase to render them.

2. `lib-apptabs` module skeleton (`framework/android/lib-apptabs`, id `ai.amberx.axf.apptabs`): settings group "App tabs" (tab list on/off, custom tabs), the same settings keys as the web plugin (`app-tabs.tabs|custom|active`) so a choice made on the web console applies on the phone once settings sync from axHub lands; action `app-tabs.show:<id>`; tab bar composable in slot `app.frame.top` (console tab = the app itself).

3. Built-in tab list on Android: Console (self), Pilot (https://pilot.amberxai.com), axHub (https://axhub.amberxai.com/apps), Demo; plus project manifests built on/for AXF with `deploy.url` read from the bundled catalog; icons from the widget icon set.

4. Locked-down web view composable `AxfWebTab`: allowed hosts only (own domains from the manifest / settings; any other link is refused with a toast — no outside browser), JavaScript on, no file access, no popups, no geolocation, mixed content blocked, `FLAG_SECURE` honoured, per-tab state kept while switching (one WebView per tab, lazily created, retained across recompositions).

5. Hub session in the app: cookie jar scoped to the app (`CookieManager`, never backed up — `android:allowBackup` rules + `dataExtractionRules`), sign-in happens on the hub's own login page inside the tab (same as the AXHub app: no JS injection, no off-hub navigation), sign-out clears cookies for every tab; the console tab's own token stays in the SecureStore.
6. Downloads: only axHub's Apps page APK links are allowed, handed to Android's DownloadManager with the hub cookie (as the AXHub app does); everything else is refused with a toast.

7. Cover slot behaviour: active non-console tab fills `app.frame.cover` below the bar; back button goes back inside the web view first, then returns to the Console tab; pull-to-refresh; a "Loading…" bar and a plain error card (offline, 4xx/5xx, refused frame) with Retry.

8. Settings → Plugins → App tabs on Android: pick tabs, add a custom tab (name + https address on an allowed host), order, reset; reuses the shared settings groups contract (`SettingsGroup`/`SettingSpec`), parent = Plugins.

9. Install in the Android console showcase (`apps/console`) and the `android-compose` template (behind a template option `--app-tabs`, default off for new apps; on for the console), manifest module list, catalog `plugins.json` entry, status.json + tracker.

10. Tests: `lib-apptabs` unit tests (allowed-host rule, settings key parity with the web plugin, tab list from manifests), Compose UI test for the bar + cover, CI job `:lib-apptabs:testDebugUnitTest`; rebuild log line, differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/console-android-app-tabs.md`, Android screenshots via `rebuild-shots.yml` on branch `fable/console-android-app-tabs`.

items.title: Console Android app: native Pilot + axHub tabs (no web content)
items.detail: Brett, Oct 20 2026: option B — Build Pilot and the axHub admin pages running natively in the Android console app (Compose), no web views. This is the Android version of Build Pilot (roadmap) plus a native hub admin client, built as small Fable steps that each stand alone. Depends on the pending `axhub-agent-host` for sessions and on axHub's admin API (its step 4). Work on it a little at a time: every sub prompt ships something usable.

subPrompts.text: 1. Build Pilot contract on Kotlin: port `src/pilot/contract.ts` (pilot-plugin@1 manifest checks, `servesStack`, `pluginsFor`, `compose` merge + conflicts, `BuildRequest` incl. `hidden`/`assets`) to a pure-Kotlin `axf-pilot-core` with fixtures shared with the web (`spec/fixtures/pilot-contract.json` generated from the TS reference) — the Fable rebuild `build-pilot-contract` folds in here.

2. Pilot API client: Kotlin client for Build Pilot's server (`/api/projects`, `/api/catalog`, `/assemble`, `/build`, `/apk`, `/metering/me`) over axf-network, token in the SecureStore, hub-admin sign-in reused; typed models mirroring `server/main.py`'s shapes; unit tests against a fake server.

3. Pilot plugin contract on Android: `pilot-plugin@1` web plugins have `web/index.tsx`; define the Android face (`android/` part: a Compose `steps` composable + the same `contribute`/`check` shape) and a loader that reads bundled plugin manifests; the designer runs only plugins that have an Android part (others are listed as web-only).

4. Pilot screens, part 1: Home (stacks + projects), Designer shell (steps from plugins, autosave through the API), Build step (review, assemble with the agent, build, validate, history) — generic UI only.

5. Pilot screens, part 2: Android parts for the bundled plugins one by one — `android-app` (App setup + boilerplate browser with screenshots), `look` (slot picks), `build-options`, `feature-manager` (FeatureList rows, Chrome section, Customize/Build now), `custom-features` (metered Claude).

6. Designers on Android: Banner and Toolbar designers (`src/pilot/designers.tsx` equivalents) producing the same asset@1 documents; widget pickers from the engine's app defaults (`typeLabels`/`typeIcons`).
7. Live preview on the phone: a floating phone-frame preview following the composed request (ScreenMock equivalent, theme compiled by the Kotlin theme engine), shrink to a pill, drag.
8. APK builds from the phone: Build APK → poll → download through DownloadManager → install prompt; progress widget bound to a counter.

9. axHub native client, part 1: hub admin API client (step-4 API on axHub: services, jobs, approvals, audit, users, projects) with the same session as the AXHub app; approvals list + single approval screen native (replacing the web view the AXHub app uses today), decide with the hub's CSRF rules through the API.

10. axHub native client, part 2: services (list/describe/call with JSON args, destructive confirm), jobs, audit log viewer, vault names (write-only: set/rotate), users + permissions, projects tree browser (`axhub.memory_*`), Apps page (download APKs).

11. Console Android tabs: a native tab bar (slot `app.frame.top` from `console-android-app-tabs` step 1) switching between Console, Pilot (native) and axHub (native); each tab keeps its own back stack; tab choice shared with the web console through settings-from-axHub.

12. Tests + report: fixtures for the pilot contract on three ports, fake-server tests for both clients, Compose tests per screen group, CI jobs, rebuild log line, differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/console-android-native-tabs.md`, screenshots via `rebuild-shots.yml`.
